Work and publication architecture

Sources and internal work
Example and Tip

Example: An accepted TEI book is in source/; the unified version and the input of a rhyme study are separated.

Tip: Document the relationships. Publish a clearly identified corpus stock for new users.

Determine publication concept
Example and Tip

Example: docs/publikationskonzept.md lists target groups, scope, structure, review and release path.

Tip: Create this file before the first public data level and maintain it like the data with Git.

Check and curate data
Example and Tip

Example: The converter gets two puzzles, but loses two solutions. An inventory comparison reports the loss, although the puzzle counting succeeds.

Tip: Connect schema/weiss check with inventory comparison and targeted source reading.

GitHub: Data, rules, examples
Example and Tip

Example: README leads from data/tei via docs/auszeichnung.md to the first call in examples/.

Tip: Let an external person try this way without personal introduction.

Release and Archive
Example and Tip

Example: Tag v1.1, release notes and archived package denote the same verified version.

Tip: Check package, metadata and version proof. One day alone is not independent archiving.

→
Local research and reporting
Example and Tip

Example: Elif downloads v1.0, performs an evaluation and reports a missing solution reference as an issue.

Tip: Ask for data version and affected identification so that the findings can be understood.

Decision paths and data flows as text

Sources and internal research lead through an early publication concept for examination and curation. The public repo provides released data, rules and examples. Releases are archived independently. Researchers work locally with designated versions and report back corrections or new annotations; their adoption requires testing and maintenance capacity again.
